==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:réactionnaire|:af<surf>|reaction|-ary|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|réactionnaire}}, equivalent to {{af|en|reaction|-ary}}.<ref>{{quote-web|accessdate=2024-07-14 04:00:21|lang=en|worklang=en|work=Oxford English Dictionary Online|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240630115635/https://www.oed.com/dictionary/reactionary_n?tab=factsheet&tl=true#26814789|archivedate=30 June 2024|url=https://www.oed.com/dictionary/reactionary_n?tab=factsheet#26814789|text=OED's earliest evidence for reactionary is from 1799, in Reply L. N. M. Carnot to Rep. Conspiracy 18th Fructidor (page 149).|title=Archived copy}}</ref> Used in the time of the French revolution to refer to a person opposing the revolution; as in favoring a {{m|en|reaction}} against the revolution.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹiˈækʃən.ɹi/|/ɹiˈækʃ(ə)nəɹi/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-reactionary.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹiˈækʃəˌnɛɹi/|a=GA}}
* {{hyphenation|en|re|ac|tion|ary}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|politics}} Extremely {{l|en|conservative}}; opposing {{l|en|revolution}} (such as the [[French Revolution]]); favoring a [[return]] to a "[[golden age]]" of the past.
#: {{syn|en|antiprogressive|regressive}}
#: {{ant|en|progressive|nonreactionary}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|date=2011-09-29
|title=The '''Reactionary''' Mind: Conservatism from Edmund Burke to Sarah Palin
|author=Corey Robin
|location=New York
|publisher=Oxford University Press
|isbn=9780199793747
|ol=25101368M
|page=25
|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=CWxIz_Gm9WMC&pg=PA25&dq=reactionary
|passage=There's a fairly simple reason for the embrace of radicalism on the right, and it has to do with the '''reactionary''' imperative that lies at the core of conservative doctrine. {{...}} If he is to preserve what he values, the conservative must declare war against the culture as it is.
}}
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|journal=w:Jewish Currents
|date=2019-8-7
|title=The Right Kind of Continuity
|url=https://jewishcurrents.org/the-right-kind-of-continuity/
|author=Marissa Brostoff; Noah Kulwin
|passage=[Jeffrey] Epstein was interested in transhumanism, a theory of human perfection via technological manipulation that—like its predecessor, eugenics—is shot through with racist and '''reactionary''' ideas.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114172543/https://jewishcurrents.org/the-right-kind-of-continuity}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|author=w:Michelle Goldberg|title=Nick Fuentes Is Becoming Charlie Kirk’s Successor|date=2025-11-04|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/03/opinion/nick-fuentes-kirk-successor.html|passage=Within certain MAGA circles, to criticize someone for being too racist or '''reactionary''' is a betrayal, signaling an acceptance of the very liberal morality that the movement’s vanguard seeks to destroy.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260206063540/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/03/opinion/nick-fuentes-kirk-successor.html|archivedate=6 February 2026}}
# {{lb|en|chemistry}} Of, pertaining to, participating in{{,}} or [[induce|inducing]] a [[chemical reaction]].
#* {{quote-web|en|date=2013-04-11|author=Brandon Smith|title=Are Individuals The Property Of The Collective?|work=Alt-Market|url=http://www.alt-market.com/articles/1437-are-individuals-the-property-of-the-collective
|passage=Psychiatry extends the theory into biology in the belief that all human behavior is nothing more than a series of '''reactionary''' chemical processes in the brain that determine pre-coded genetic responses built up from the conditioning of one’s environment.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305103115/https://www.alt-market.com/articles/1437-are-individuals-the-property-of-the-collective}}
# In reaction to; as a result of.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|politics}} One who opposes [[revolution]], wanting to reverse it, favoring a return to a past [[golden age]], often used [[derogatorily]] by [[revolutionary|revolutionaires]].
#* {{RQ:New York|author=Andrew Sullivan|year=2017|month=April|title=The Reactionary Temptation|url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2017/04/andrew-sullivan-why-the-reactionary-right-must-be-taken-seriously.html|passage=It is not simply a conservative preference for things as they are, with a few nudges back, but a passionate loathing of the status quo and a desire to return to the past in one emotionally cathartic revolt. If conservatives are pessimistic, '''reactionaries''' are apocalyptic.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200415094857/https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2017/04/andrew-sullivan-why-the-reactionary-right-must-be-taken-seriously.html}}
